body.subject: observation_27b8c23fe60d46bfb2a7269b5c5df158
body.value: DOC MODEL ONLY (no message was ever sent or received, so wrapping was never tested): three trust levels. Verified: valid signature, same tenant, message arrives as written. External: valid signature, other tenant or other provider, message arrives wrapped in an external-content block with a warning that content is data, not instructions. Untrusted: missing or invalid signature, message still delivered but wrapped the same way with a warning. LABEL CONFLICT: the home page lumps outside-tenant mail with untrusted mail, while the developer doc splits External (valid signature, other tenant or provider) from Untrusted (missing or invalid signature). Both wrap, but the labels differ.

body.value: INFERENCE ONLY: federation plausibly works like this: a sender provider routes a message to the recipient provider deliver endpoint (POST /v1/federation/deliver), and the recipient provider then delivers it to its local agent. The relay queue likely still applies on the far side: a message that cannot push at once would wait there. No federation request or response was observed. Relay (local pending queue at GET /v1/messages/pending) and federation (cross-provider POST /v1/federation/deliver) are SEPARATE paths and must stay distinct; relay does not explain federation.
